Abstract:

Fibroblast growth factor receptors (FGFRs) are a family of receptor tyrosine kinases that regulate diverse biological events, including cell proliferation, differentiation, migration and survival. Deregulated FGFR signalling plays a vital role in cancer development and progression. Among the genomic aberrations affecting FGFRs, chromosomal rearrangements that generate FGFR fusion genes are of particular interest, as fusion-driven tumours have been shown to respond to targeted therapy. Efficient and accurate identification of such fusions is therefore essential for determining treatment strategies and prognosis. The present study was undertaken to design and develop CRISPR/Cas13d and CRISPR/Cas12a based systems for the targeting and detection of FGFR2 fusion genes. Guide RNA constructs specific to FGFR2 fusion transcripts were designed and cloned for Cas13d mediated oncogenic RNA targeting, with cloning carried out using standard molecular cloning techniques. In parallel, guide RNA primers spanning the FGFR2 fusion region were designed for Cas12a based detection of the fusion genes. The study successfully generated cloned Cas13d gRNA constructs and fusion-specific guide RNA primers for Cas12a mediated detection. Together, these findings demonstrate the feasibility of employing CRISPR based platforms for both therapeutic RNA targeting and molecular diagnostics of FGFR2 fusion genes. Keywords: Fusion gene, CRISPR/Cas13d, oncogenic RNA targeting
